- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.4) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.4), adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 10–15 day average, not extreme highs/lows.  
- Overshoots after spikes (forecast > true by >5%) are common in positive sentiment; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day high to prevent runaway inflation.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is weak or neutral, forecast should be closer to 14-day moving average, not 30-day trend.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.2) over 3–5 days, suppress upward momentum in forecast; if sentiment is consistently high (≥ 0.8), allow slight upward bias but cap at 1.2x recent peak.
